talk_track: Daniel Kirichanski here — I ran cloud operations for an Industrial AI platform at Avathon and cut MTTR roughly 40% at Tricentis by putting AI agents into incident detection and root-cause analysis, the same mandate your live Lead DevOps Engineer posting describes. That posting asks one lead engineer to 'own the DevOps function end-to-end across the entire company' — GitLab, EKS across AWS and GCP, security tooling, an internal developer platform, plus 'LLM-assisted root cause analysis, alert summarization, and runbook generation to reduce mean time to resolution.' That is a platform organization's charter written as a single CA$145–185K role. Read plainly, it means the AI-enabled engineering transformation has no senior owner between the Head of Technology and the ICs, and while the req sits open, delivery friction and multi-cloud spend keep compounding. Whoever fills it will need an operating model on day one — DORA baselines, a FinOps loop, and an evaluation harness before more AI tooling gets embedded. Which is hurting more right now — delivery friction or cloud spend?
